title: Anthropic Research Resident
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>About Anthropic</strong></h2> <p>Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.</p></div><h2><strong>About the role</strong></h2> <p>The Anthropic Residency is our paid, fixed-term research program, with placements lasting between six weeks and six months. We are looking for people who have led ambitious work in a variety of technical fields and want to transition to full-time work focused on making sure AI systems are safe and beneficial for all of humanity. If you are a <strong>professor in a quantitative discipline, a technical founder or a staff-level engineer</strong> and want to transition to work on transformative AI, we want to hear from you. Background in machine learning is not required.</p> <h2><strong>What to expect</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A concrete, scoped project matched to your background, with direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers</li> <li>Access to Claude models and GPU compute</li> <li>Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Interview process</strong></h2> <p>The interview process will include an initial application, recruiter screen, technical assessment, research discussion and a reference check.</p> <p>Applications for this round close on November 22, 2026 (11:59 PM PT). We expect to make offers in January 2027.</p> <h2><strong>You may be a good fit if you</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole</li> <li>Are excited to transition into working on empirical AI research full-time</li> <li>Have led ambitious work in a variety of technical fields (professor in a quantitative discipline, a technical founder or a staff-level engineer)</li> <li>Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments</li> <li>Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Strong candidates may also</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Have experience authoring research papers in machine learning, NLP, or AI safety</li> <li>Have experience with LLMs, reinforcement learning or Kubernetes clusters and complex shared codebases</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Mentors and research areas</strong></h2> <p>Potential Anthropic mentors include:</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/sara-price-310757b2/">Sara Price</a>: leads the Alignment Training team; background in data science</li> <li><a href="https://ethanperez.net/">Ethan Perez</a>: leads the Alignment Science team; background in machine learning</li> <li><a href="https://evhub.github.io/">Evan Hubinger</a>: leads the Alignment Stress-Testing team; formerly at The Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)</li> <li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=fW7yK10AAAAJ&hl=en">Samuel Marks</a>: leads the Scalable Oversight team; background in mathematics</li> <li><a href="https://elanapearl.github.io/">Elana Simon</a>: researches the interpretability of language models and biological models; background in biomedical informatics</li> <li><a href="https://belindal.github.io/">Belinda Li</a>: researches how language models represent the world, users, and themselves; background in natural language processing (PhD, MIT)</li> <li><a href="https://jlindsey15.github.io/">Jack Lindsey</a>: leads the Model Psychology team; background in theoretical neuroscience</li> <li><a href="https://nicholas.carlini.com/">Nicholas Carlini</a>: researches adversarial machine learning and AI security; previously at DeepMind and Google Brain</li> <li><a href="https://sohldickstein.com/">Jascha Sohl-Dickstein</a>: works at the intersection of safety and pretraining; background in physics and neuroscience, formerly Principal Scientist at Google Brain</li> </ul> <p>Residents will work on empirical research questions in collaboration with Anthropic's research teams. Areas we are particularly interested in include:</p> <p>AI safety & alignment</p> <ul> <li>Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains.</li> <li>Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios.</li> <li>Model Organisms: Creating <a href="https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/ChDH335ckdvpxXaXX/model-organisms-of-misalignment-the-case-for-a-new-pillar-of-1">model organisms of misalignment</a> to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.</li> <li>Model Internals and Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.</li> <li>Safeguards Research: Developing robust defenses against adversarial attacks, comprehensive evaluation frameworks for model safety, and automated systems to detect and mitigate potential risks before deployment.</li> <li>AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.</li> </ul> <p>AI security & frontier red-teaming</p> <ul> <li>Stress-testing frontier models to understand the full extent of their current capabilities in fields such as cybersecurity, robotics or cryptography.</li> </ul> <p>ML systems & reinforcement learning</p> <ul> <li>Improving how frontier models are trained and building the infrastructure behind that research, from model architecture, optimizers and training data to accelerator simulators, hardware backends and RL environment pipelines.</li> </ul> <p>For a fuller picture of the questions we care about, see our <a href="https://alignment.anthropic.com/2025/recommended-directions/">Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions</a> and recent publications from our <a href="https://alignment.anthropic.com/">Alignment</a>, <a href="https://transformer-circuits.pub/">Interpretability</a> and <a href="https://red.anthropic.com/">Frontier Red</a> teams.</p> <h2><strong>Logistics</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Duration:</strong> Placements are six weeks, three months or six months, depending on team fit and candidate preferences. Other lengths between three and six months are possible by exception.</li> <li><strong>Location:</strong> This application is for a remote UK position, with the option to work from our London office. However, we prefer that Residents work from our San Francisco office, where most of our research staff is based, but remote participation is possible, especially for shorter placements. Most full-time research roles at Anthropic require relocation to San Francisco. Remote participants need to be based in a country where Anthropic can hire.</li> <li><strong>Commitment:</strong> Full-time role for the duration of the residency.</li> <li><strong>Compensation:</strong> £265,000 to £375,000/year pro-rated for the duration of the residency + benefits</li> <li><strong>Visa sponsorship:</strong> We sponsor visas for placements of three months or longer. For six-week placements we encourage remote participation from a country where Anthropic can hire.</li> </ul> <p>Applicants may also be considered for the <a href="https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/anthropic/jobs/5183044008">Anthropic Fellows Program</a>.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p>The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. </p> <p>For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.</p></div><div class="title">Annual Salary:</div><div class="pay-range"><span>£265,000</span><span class="divider">—</span><span>£375,000 GBP</span></div></div></div><div class="content-conclusion"><h2><strong>Logistics</strong></h2> <p><strong>Minimum education: </strong>Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience</p> <p><strong>Required field of study: </strong>A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience</p> <p><strong>Minimum years of experience: </strong>Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position</p> <p><strong>Location-based hybrid policy:</strong> Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.</p> <p><strong data-stringify-type="bold">Visa sponsorship:</strong> We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.</p> <p><strong>We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.</strong> Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.<br><br><strong data-stringify-type="bold">Your safety matters to us.</strong> To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit <u data-stringify-type="underline"><a class="c-link c-link--underline" href="http://anthropic.com/careers" target="_blank" data-stringify-link="http://anthropic.com/careers" data-sk="tooltip_parent" data-remove-tab-index="true">anthropic.com/career

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer, Front-end Focus - Growth

title: Account Executive (UK)
description: About SINGU At SINGU , we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide , supporting more than 500,000 professionals. You've closed complex six-figure deals with multiple stakeholders, procurement and IT security reviews. This isn't high-volume transactional sales. Sector knowledge in warehousing, logistics, industrial or supply chain, or in facilities management software. If your background is in commercial real estate, we'd want to see a very strong sales track record. A track record you can walk us through. What you sold, to whom, how you got in, and what you said. We value an honest career story over polished numbers. If you've had a quarter or a year that didn't go to plan, we want to hear what you did about it. C-level credibility. You can build a business case and defend it in front of a finance audience. MEDDICC or a similar qualification framework, used in practice. Understanding of the UK market , and the energy to build something as the new-business team grows. What we offer Base salary, uncapped commission and accelerators. Dedicated Solution Consulting, BD support and marketing programmes aimed at your segment. A real path into enterprise sales leadership as the team scales. Remote working, with roughly monthly time together in London or Birmingham. Logistics Location: UK, remote (England or Wales preferred) Travel: roughly monthly to London or Birmingham Employment type: Full-time If this role sounds like a good fit, we’d love to hear from you. Apply and help us build technology that supports critical operations every day. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Colleagues across Sona will be running the product, operations and other launch activities, so your focus is winning customers, building partnerships and creating the collateral to sell. title: Regional Director of Operations, UK, Europe and Africa
description: Regional Director of Operations, UK, Europe and Africa Kenyon International Emergency Services, part of the TrustFlight Group Bracknell, United Kingdom | Full time, permanent | Competitive salary and benefits package When the worst happens, families need someone they can trust. Lead that response. When an aircraft is lost, a ship is in distress or a community is struck by disaster, families are suddenly facing the hardest days of their lives. They need answers, they need to be treated with dignity, and they need to know that the people they have lost are being cared for. For more than a century, Kenyon International Emergency Services has been the organisation that airlines, governments and major companies call on to make sure that happens. We are looking for a senior crisis leader to direct that response across the UK, Europe and Africa. This is a role for someone who has stood in the room when it mattered, who leads with calm authority, and who believes that how an organisation treats the bereaved and the injured says everything about its character. About Kenyon Kenyon provides emergency planning, family assistance, humanitarian support and recovery services to clients around the world, drawing on a network of more than 2,500 trained responders who can be mobilised at short notice into any jurisdiction. Our clients rely on us to keep their promises to the people affected by an incident, and we hold ourselves to that standard every day, not only on the day of an activation. Kenyon is part of the TrustFlight Group, an aviation safety and compliance technology business. That gives Kenyon something unusual in this sector: a world class technology team working alongside it, and a genuine commitment to using AI to make crisis response faster, better informed and more humane. Our values are simple and we mean them: integrity, and a customer first attitude in everything we do. The role Kenyon operates a two hub leadership model. You will lead the Bracknell hub, with regional accountability for operational delivery, readiness, contracted offices and relationships across the UK, Europe and Africa. Your peer, the Regional Director of Operations in Vancouver, leads the Americas and Asia Pacific. Together you share accountability for the readiness and quality of Kenyon’s response worldwide. Senior Incident Director for activations Senior on call duty is shared between the two Directors on a fixed twelve hour rota, with a structured handover at each change of duty, so that cover is continuous around the clock and neither Director works through their own night. Your window runs from approximately 06:00 to 18:00 UK time. When an incident arises during your window, wherever in the world it occurs, you take up the role of Senior Incident Director. You will have the authority to set the deployment posture, commit responders and stand the organisation up or down without further approval. Where a client requires it, you will deploy as their strategic point of contact, leading the response on their behalf at the most demanding moments an organisation can face, including mass casualty, government led and politically sensitive events. Major activations are infrequent, and Kenyon holds its capability through a surge based model rather than a large permanent workforce. Your judgement of regional readiness, kept current every week of the year, is what makes that model work. What you will lead · Regional readiness and response. Maintain and continuously measure activation readiness across the UK, Europe and Africa, and develop the procedures, protocols and contingency plans that underpin it. · Your team and offices. Line manage the Regional Operations Manager in Bracknell, run the Bracknell hub and its regional operations as one regional function, and hold contracted offices to defined standards through quarterly reviews and an annual assessment. · Protecting those we serve. Make sure the information of casualties, families and clients is protected with the same care during and after an activation as on any other day. · The responder network. Work with the Responder Manager to keep the network vetted, trained and available across the region, including building language capable responders across Europe and Africa. Own the global standards for responder vetting, training currency, deployment conduct and post incident review, ensuring they are consistently applied across both hubs. · AI and digital quality assurance. Work with the Vancouver Director and TrustFlight Group technology team to define and evaluate AI enabled quality and operational reporting tools, including an AI internal auditor supporting ISO 9001, ISO 27001 and ISO 22300 evidence gathering, gap identification and audit trail maintenance. Ensure these tools meet group information security, data governance and ethical standards. · Global operational standards. Work with the Vancouver Director to compare regional procedures, share lessons learned and adopt improvements across both hubs, ensuring consistent service quality while recognising regional operational requirements. · Relationships that matter. Build trusted working relationships with government agencies, emergency services, aviation authorities and clients across the region, and provide the operational insight that informs board level reporting. Why join us · Work that matters. Few roles offer the chance to lead a service whose sole purpose is to bring order, care and dignity to people at the worst moment of their lives. · Real authority. A senior seat on the Kenyon leadership team, reporting to the Managing Director, with decision making authority during activations. · A sustainable model. A shared rota designed so that no Director carries standing 24/7 availability, because sound judgement depends on rest. · Room to build. The opportunity to shape Kenyon’s growth across the UK, Europe and Africa, while leading the development of global quality, certification and responder standards and helping shape how AI strengthens operational assurance across Kenyon. In your cover letter, tell us about an incident you have led and what it taught you about caring for the people affected. Applications will be treated in strict confidence. Kenyon International Emergency Services and TrustFlight are equal opportunity employers. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and will make reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process for anyone who needs them. This position is employed by Kenyon International Emergency Services Limited. What you will bring · At least ten years in operational crisis management or emergency response, including five or more in a leadership role. · Experience leading large scale or complex incident responses in international environments, ideally including direct responsibility for strategic command. · A track record of managing contracted service providers against defined performance standards. · Experience working within a quality management framework in a regulated or standards led environment, and alongside board level governance. · The composure, judgement and compassion to lead when the stakes are highest, and the humility to put the needs of affected families first. · Willingness to travel internationally at short notice, including to the United States and across Asia Pacific. · Eligibility to live and work in the UK. It would be a real advantage if you also have · Professional fluency in Spanish, or another principal European and African language. · Familiarity with the ISO 22300 series, including ISO 22320, or equivalent certification experience. · Experience overseeing a 24/7 contact centre operation. · Practical experience commissioning AI or automation tools in an operational setting. · Knowledge of the aviation, maritime, energy or government crisis response markets in the Europe and Africa. title: Group Director of Supply Chain
description: Why A‑Gas? At A‑Gas, what we do matters — every single day. We are a global leader in Lifecycle Refrigerant Management. We help industries reduce emissions, protect the environment, and transition to a more sustainable future. Our goal is clear: to protect and improve the environment by effectively managing refrigerants throughout their entire lifecycle. Role Description The Group Director, Supply Chain is accountable for designing and leading A-Gas's global supply chain, strategic sourcing and Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning (SIOP) capability. The role will create an integrated view of demand, supply, inventory and third-party spend to secure critical supply, improve service, optimise inventory and working capital, reduce total cost and enable better commercial and operational decisions. Key spend categories include gases, valves, cylinders and containers, logistics, maintenance, repair and operations (MRO), and selected indirect categories. Working through a global matrix of regional Operations, Purchasing, Commercial and Finance teams, the role will establish common governance, data standards, category strategies and performance measures while enabling effective regional execution. The role operates through a global matrix structure. While accountable for Group strategy, governance, performance and capability, day-to-day execution remains with regional procurement, Commercial, Operations and supply chain teams. Reports to Group Operations Director Principal Place of Work United Kingdom or United States - home-based or hybrid by agreement, with regular travel to A-Gas sites, suppliers and international meetings. Experience, Knowledge and Qualifications Essential Significant senior leadership experience across strategic sourcing, procurement and supply chain planning in a complex, multi-region organisation. Demonstrable experience designing or materially improving S&OP/SIOP processes Proven delivery of measurable value across direct and indirect categories. Strong commercial, negotiation and financial analysis capability. Experience leading enterprise change through a matrix. Strong understanding of supplier risk, logistics, inventory and supply continuity. Experience using ERP, CRM, planning and spend analytics data. Desirable Industrial gases, chemicals, refrigerants, hazardous materials or regulated-sector experience. Dangerous goods logistics, international sourcing and trade compliance experience. Experience in a private equity-backed, acquisitive or high-growth organisation. APICS/ASCM, CIPS, CPSM or another relevant qualification. Experience implementing sourcing, procure-to-pay or planning technology What do you get in return? Competitive and attractive employment package Employer pension scheme Flexible working hours (depending on the role) Collective benefits program Employee Assistance Program (support for work and personal matters) Cycle to work scheme Team activities in summer and around Christmas Why choose A‑Gas? Because your work contributes to something bigger: A safer climate A more sustainable industry An organization with a clear mission, innovative strength, and long-term vision Together, we are building a sustainable future. title: Customer Value Architect III
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About Mixpanel</strong></p> <p>Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at <a href="https://mixpanel.com/home/">mixpanel.com</a>.</p></div><p><strong>About the Role</strong></p> <p><strong><em>Not a technical role, despite 'architect' in the title, this is relationship and strategy work, not engineering. Customer success, account management, or consulting backgrounds are a better fit than technical ones.</em></strong></p> <p>The right candidate is a relationship-first advisor who thrives on connecting customers' Mixpanel investment to real business outcomes. You'll be the consultative owner of adoption, value, and AI maturity across a named portfolio of high-value accounts, engaged from onboarding through the full contract lifecycle. You are accountable for the outcome, not the commercial relationship owning the value case and the adoption plan behind it. You will build the executive relationships and strategic plans that make Mixpanel indispensable to how your customers build products.</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Connect mixpanel to customer value</strong> <ul> <li>Own our value workstream with customers - understanding the business challenges that led them to buy Mixpanel, how they measure the ROI of their investment, and ensuring that they achieve that ROI by working across the customers’ teams and collaborating internally with other Mixpanel teams.</li> <li>Build and own relationships across business and technical stakeholders, including executive sponsors, aligning Mixpanel's capabilities to customers' highest-priority goals.</li> <li>Develop and execute success plans that map customer business objectives to adoption milestones and measurable outcomes.</li> <li>Perform ongoing discovery of the customer’s business priorities, internal toolset, and ongoing business pain – synthesize this information into actions that feed your success plans and share information with internal partners as needed.</li> <li>Operate in lockstep with the AE and renewal team, with clear lanes: you partner with the AE on expansion and growth motions and with the renewal team on renewal execution, bringing the value case and adoption evidence that underpins both. You own the value case; they own the commercial outcome.</li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Own value delivery and product relationship </strong> <ul> <li>Lead customer enablement sessions—covering topics like dashboard design, funnel analysis, and retention modeling—to grow Mixpanel usage depth and breadth across the customer organization.</li> <li>Proactively monitor product usage and health signals; lead regular business reviews to surface insights, deepen adoption, and surface risk early.</li> <li>Drive customer adoption - title: Head of Solution Consulting R&D / Field CSO
description: We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era. When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done. Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma. We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today. WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW R&D leaders trust people who have done the science. More than half of the world's top 50 biopharma companies already use Benchling, and many of the most important are in Europe. Our ambition is 10x faster science, from idea to first dose. With Science Foundries, launched at Benchtalk 2026, agents and scientists run entire R&D workflows together, so a three-person team can have the productive capacity of thirty. In a senior R&D role, you can change how one organisation does science. As our Field CSO, you'll take one question to R&D organisations across EMEA: how do we get from idea to first dose 10x faster? ROLE OVERVIEW You'll lead our EMEA R&D Solution Consulting organisation: a team of 12, with two first-line leaders covering our Enterprise and Strategic segments, plus occasional support for APAC deals. You'll be the scientific counterpart to our General Manager, EMEA, and work alongside our Field CTO. They lead on IT, data science and architecture; you lead on the scientists and how their work changes. RESPONSIBILITIES Be the scientific voice in the room. Brief the GM and account teams before key meetings, then join them as a peer to the CSOs and Heads of R&D across the table. Act as senior sponsor on our largest EMEA opportunities, and use account-team introductions to open new R&D relationships. Lead the 10x conversation. Turn Benchling's vision, from AI agents to Science Foundries, into a credible plan R&D leaders can act on, including how their scientists move onto Benchling and what changes in the lab. Lead and develop two first-line leaders and their team of 10. Provide in-region leadership continuity, set the scientific bar for every customer engagement, and build a succession plan as the team grows. Shape EMEA strategy and the roadmap. Decide with sales leadership where to focus the team's expertise, and bring patterns from the field back to Product, Marketing and global Solution Consulting. HOW WE'LL MEASURE SUCCESS This is a commercial role with a scientific core. We'll look at EMEA revenue growth and influenced pipeline, technical win rate, forecast accuracy on the technical side of deals, regional ownership of our largest R&D relationships, and the strength of your leadership bench. QUALIFICATIONS Substantial hands-on R&D experience in biotech or pharma, with a PhD or equivalent scientific depth. You've run experiments, led programmes and know how large R&D organisations make decisions and adopt change. A record of driving change, from adopting new technologies to rethinking how your teams work, and clear views on how AI will change R&D. Experience leading through other managers, and executive presence with VPs, Heads of R&D and C-level leaders. Commercial ambition and a growth mindset. We'll teach you how software is sold. We can't teach how a large R&D organisation works from the inside, and that's what you bring. Readiness for a field role: frequent on-site time with the largest pharma and biotech companies across EMEA, plus US travel three to four times a year for team offsites and our global sales kickoff. Fluency in English; German or French is a plus. NICE TO HAVE Experience with Benchling or a comparable R&D platform (ELN, LIMS or R&D data platform), including leading its evaluation or rollout Customer-facing scientific, internal consulting, or CRO/CDMO programme leadership roles Presales or solution consulting experience HOW WE WORK We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday). #LI-Hybrid #BI-Hybrid Benchling welcomes everyone. We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences. We are an equal opportunity employer. That means we don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. title: GTM Engineer
description: About Kernel Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this? Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier. Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust. Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them. We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 12x YoY . The Role We're looking for a GTM Engineer to build the systems that take Kernel to $100m+ ARR. You'll own the infrastructure behind how we find, sell to and grow customers, from Salesforce and outbound to forecasting, renewals and expansion. This is a hands-on builder role, not a traditional RevOps support function. You'll work like a product engineer for GTM: find the biggest constraint on growth, turn a messy commercial problem into a working system, ship it quickly and improve it using real results. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you do need to be able to build with Salesforce, Clay, APIs, automation platforms and AI tools rather than waiting for someone else to do it. You'll also be Kernel's own internal customer , using Kernel to build an AI-native revenue engine, pressure-test the product in real workflows and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering. You'll report to Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations , and work closely with Sales leadership and the wider GTM team. What You'll Be Doing Build a better outbound engine: improve account targeting, signals, enrichment, prioritization, personalization, sequencing and measurement so the team consistently reaches the right companies at the right time Make the GTM team more productive: automate repetitive work across account research, meeting preparation, follow-ups, CRM hygiene and handoffs so BDRs, AEs and Account Managers spend more time with customers Run the revenue operating infrastructure: own the systems behind pipeline management, forecasting, funnel reporting, quota planning, GTM incentive compensation, renewals and expansion Set the rules of engagement: own account assignment and routing, settle ownership disputes, and make sure every meeting booked and held is captured and credited to the right person Improve how revenue work moves through Kernel: build reliable routing, attribution, account assignment and cross-functional handoffs, resolve edge cases and make performance visible Be Kernel's own internal customer: deploy Kernel on our CRM, use it to improve our GTM data and workflows, and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering What You Bring 3-5 years of relevant experience: you have worked in RevOps, Sales Ops or GTM Engineering at a high-growth Series B-E SaaS company and owned meaningful parts of the revenue engine end to end Deep Salesforce fluency: you understand objects, record types, fields, formulas, flows, validation rules, permissions, reports and data migration. You can reason about architecture and debug production behavior Strong GTM building ability: you have built useful systems with Clay, APIs, automation platforms and AI tools, and you know how to move from a rough idea to a reliable workflow that people adopt Commercial judgment: you understand how accounts become meetings, meetings become pipeline, pipeline is qualified and forecast, and won revenue flows into implementation, expansion, renewal and retention Strong data instincts: you can turn fragmented information into trustworthy workflows, measure what is working and create feedback loops that improve performance over time Clear, low-ego communication: you can turn a messy request into a crisp decision, explain trade-offs to non-technical teams, push back constructively and drive adoption through influence rather than authority It is a plus if you also have: Experience supporting an enterprise sales motion with multi-stakeholder deals and MEDDPICC Experience with renewals, expansion, compensation, quota setting or planning Familiarity with Gong, sales engagement platforms and modern enrichment or intent tooling Experience building operational controls around LLM- or agent-powered workflows ⚠️ This role may not be for you if you: Prefer strategy and recommendations over configuring systems, cleaning data, investigating edge cases and debugging workflows yourself Need outlined requirements or stable priorities before you can make progress See GTM Engineering primarily as CRM administration or ticket fulfillment rather than a revenue-generating function ❌ This role is definitely not for you if you: Are not comfortable taking broad ownership of a function Prefer a predictable, low-intensity environment Want to protect a 9-to-6 or a mostly remote setup. We are in the office together 4-5 days a week and the pace is high What We Offer We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling. 💰 Salary: £70,000-£90,000 + equity 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays 🥕 £450 monthly office dinner allowance ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere 🍼 Generous parental leave policy 💼 Pension plan 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office 🎉 Team events and dinners 🚀 Work directly with the founders to build the systems that power an AI-native revenue engine 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace ❤️ Team Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations Amin Shafi, BizOps Associate Dave Bentham, Head of Sales 🎫 Visas & Relocation Not offered for this role. Interview Process Stage 1: Screening: Intro call Stage 2: Technical: In-person case interview Stage 3: Coffee chat: In-person discussion with members of our GTM team Final stage: Values: Interview with founders for culture and values alignment If there is mutual fit, we move to references and offer. title: Staff Front End Engineer

We are united by a single vision to help people live longer, healthier lives, using the power of genomics. Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time. Role Purpose Genomics turns large-scale genetic and health data into insight that speeds up drug discovery and helps people understand their risk of disease. None of it matters if people can’t explore it, trust it and act on it. As a Staff Front End Engineer, you’ll own the front end of our SaaS platform and shape how scientists, clinicians and partners interact with data at scale. You’ll report to our Engineering Manager and work closely with product, design and data teams. Compensation & Growth Competitive Reward: Salaries are externally benchmarked annually to ensure market-aligned compensation. Clear Career Path: A straightforward, open progression framework means you’ll always know the path to promotion and how to achieve your next career goal. Continuous Learning: Including external courses and a wide library of L&D materials, because your growth is our success. Wellbeing & Time Off Holiday: 25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays, plus an extra 3-day company-wide shutdown at year-end. Financial & Health Security: Robust benefits including a market-leading pension scheme, comprehensive private health insurance for you and your family with NO excess, critical illness, and life assurance. Enhanced Leave: Enhanced paid family leave to support all new parents. Work Environment & Culture Hybrid Working Truly Inclusive Time Off: Our ‘Bank Your Bank Holiday’ program allows you to exchange public holidays for dates that hold personal or cultural significance to you. Vibrant Social Culture: From regular Town Halls and team picnics to organised sports events, our social committee ensures frequent opportunities to connect and celebrate. Green Commute: Cycle-to-Work scheme and convenient office locations near major transport hubs. Ready to Build the Future? If this opportunity excites you, apply now! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. title: UK I Fractional Legal Counsel
description: About Infinite Lambda Infinite Lambda is a global data and AI consultancy on a mission to make innovation accessible. We help organisations build the data foundations and business context they need for enterprise AI to actually work: from modern data platforms to agentic enablement and our software solution, Flowline. We are a Certified B Corporation, with 7 legal entities around the world, and are proud to nurture a workplace where decent human beings can do their best work. Curiosity is our default setting, autonomy is non-negotiable, and impact is the whole point. The role As our Fractional Legal Counsel, you will be the senior legal partner to our COO, Exec team, and Board. In a fractional capacity, you will be part of the team, close to the people who win and deliver the work, and trusted to make the calls that keep us keep moving. We need someone who can start adding value from their first week. You will handle our most important contracts and legal questions across EMEA, the Americas, and APAC, and set up the templates, playbooks, and processes that let the business handle routine matters with confidence when you are not there. Being qualified in both England & Wales and the US means you can cover our two largest legal systems directly and coordinate local counsel everywhere else. You will report to the COO and work closely with our CFO and General Managers, as many of our legal questions (commercial terms, liability, entity structure and governance) sit at the intersection of legal, finance, and operations. As the business grows, you will also help us decide what our long-term legal function should look like. What you will own This role spans four pillars. As the role is fractional, focus matters a lot: you will prioritise what only a senior lawyer can do, bring in external support where it makes sense, and build the tools that let the business help itself. 1. Commercial contracting & client advice Reviewing and negotiating our priority client agreements: MSAs, SOWs and framework agreements under English and US law Drafting key partner, vendor, and supplier agreements Advising clients and internal teams on cross-border matters across EMEA, the Americas, and APAC Setting clear positions on liability, IP ownership, and data terms, so deals keep moving 2. Governance, risk & compliance Flagging the legal risks that matter most and recommending priorities to the COO and Exec team; Oversight of corporate governance and entity matters across our 7 legal entities, working with local advisers; Supporting the Exec team and board matters when legal input is needed; Keeping our compliance posture current, including anti-bribery, sanctions, and export controls. 3. Data, AI & intellectual property Data protection and privacy across the UK, EU and US, including DPAs and international transfers; Guidance on AI regulation, including the EU AI Act, as it applies to our services; Protecting our intellectual property, including our flagship product, Flowline. 4. Building the legal foundations Contract templates, negotiation playbooks and approval rules for routine matters; A simple intake and tracking process so everyone knows what is in progress; Selecting and managing external counsel for specialist or local-law work, within budget; Helping shape the scope of a future full-time legal hire if and when we need one. Who you are We are not looking for a particular CV but for a particular kind of lawyer, namely senior, commercial, honest, and genuinely interested in the work our teams do. Experience that matters Qualified as a solicitor in England & Wales and the US (preferrably), with both qualifications current and in good standing; 7+ years' PQE, with training at a leading law firm and in-house experience, ideally in technology, data, AI or professional services; A track record of working fractionally, as an interim, or as a consultant lawyer, and of making an impact quickly; Strong commercial contracting experience, especially services, technology and SaaS agreements; Experience advising on cross-border matters across the UK, EU, and US, with exposure to APAC a plus; Working knowledge of data protection, IP, and emerging AI regulation; Experience setting up legal processes or being a company's first legal adviser; Your own professional indemnity insurance, or cover through your platform or consultancy. Your approach You prioritise ruthlessly and are clear about what can wait; You give clear answers and a recommendation, not a list of risks; You build trust with clients, colleagues and leadership because you are straight with them; You leave things better documented than you found them, so the business is never stuck waiting for you; You bring rigour without bureaucracy. Life is too short for red tape; You are aligned with our company values. This matters to us. How the engagement works 10 days a month with flexibility around specific working hours and with reasonable availability for urgent matters outside of those; A shared request channel and a simple tracker so priorities are visible to everyone; A regular check-in with the COO to review workload, priorities and whether the agreed working days still fit; Additional days agreed in advance, at the same day rate. Why work with us Being your true self : show up as you are. We work with people for character, not conformity; Practising innovation : front-row seat to the rapid evolution of data and AI, and the legal questions that come with it; Living autonomously : remote-first, with flexibility on how you structure your days; Real influence : a senior voice in a growing global business, working directly with the COO and Exec team. We are a Certified B Corporation. That means we measure ourselves not just by what we deliver, but by how we deliver it because of our people, our clients, our communities, and the environment. Our Legal Counsel will help make sure that commitment is reflected in how we contract and govern ourselves. The practicalities Engagement: Fractional, initial term of 12 months with the option to extend; Contract: Consultancy agreement, directly, through your own company, or through a fractional legal platform; IR35 status assessed before contracting; Location: Remote-first / UK / US; Reports to: COO; Key partnerships: CEO, CTO, CFO, and other Exec team members; General Managers, Sales and Partnership leads, Head of People / HR; Compensation: competitive day rate. A chain of trust from the hardware up to the rack management plane: the root of trust each controller boots from, the signed updates that reach the fleet safely, the identity that lets a device prove what it is, the authenticated channels the controllers and devices talk over, and the runtime protections that keep the host Linux kernel and the on-die firmware trustworthy long after boot. In this role, the security of your software solutions depends entirely on how well you understand the hardware beneath it. Some of the protections we rely on live in silicon, some in software, and part of the skill is knowing which belongs where. We’re looking for people who know both sides well enough to build the mechanisms that close whole classes of bugs by design. We’re not heavy on levels here! Whether you’d call yourself senior, staff, principal, or lead, what matters is depth of security judgement, system-level experience, and working well with the engineers around you. title: Engineering Manager, Guardian
description: About the Team The Guardian team builds practical safety and oversight systems for increasingly capable AI agents. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm. Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products. Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group. About the Role We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead and grow the Guardian team in London. You will own the engineering strategy and execution for production systems that evaluate agent behavior, identify risk, and take appropriate action without creating unnecessary friction for users. This is a builder-manager role with substantial technical depth. You will set direction, develop engineers, and create the operating cadence for a high-performing team, while remaining close enough to the work to shape architecture, review designs, debug difficult problems, and write code when it is the highest-leverage way to help the team move forward. The role is highly visible and cross-functional. You will work closely with alignment researchers to translate emerging research into dependable systems, and with product teams to make agent safety a foundational capability across OpenAI. This role is based in our London office. In this role, you will Lead, hire, and develop a London-based team of engineers working across agent safety, backend systems, applied AI, and product infrastructure. Set the technical roadmap for Auto-review and the broader Guardian platform, balancing safety, product utility, latency, and operational reliability. Build production systems that evaluate agent actions in real time, detect potentially harmful behavior, and support safe recovery or escalation paths. Improve how oversight systems understand user intent, environmental context, permissions, and relevant personalization signals while protecting privacy and avoiding unnecessary friction. Partner closely with alignment researchers to turn prototypes, evaluations, and new monitoring techniques into scalable product capabilities. Work across Product, Security, Infrastructure, and other engineering teams to integrate Guardian capabilities into agent experiences throughout OpenAI. Establish rigorous evaluation and operational practices, including adversarial testing, failure analysis, monitoring, and metrics for safety performance, false positives, latency, and user impact. You might thrive in this role if you Have significant experience leading engineering teams that shipped complex, high-stakes production systems end to end. Have built with AI agents or large language models in a core product, startup, or technically serious independent project, and understand the unique challenges of agentic systems. Bring strong product-engineering judgment and can navigate tradeoffs across safety, usability, speed, and reliability. Can partner effectively with research teams, translate open-ended findings into engineering plans, and communicate clearly across technical disciplines. Have a thoughtful management system for hiring, coaching, performance, and execution. Care deeply about building AI systems that are useful, trustworthy, and safe. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. title: Senior Hub Developer
description: We're looking for a developer to grow Ember's network of charging hubs. You'll find the sites, take them through legals and planning, manage the build and energise them. How you work and think matters more to us than which industry you've worked in. You think clearly, can run several projects at once and are as at home on a site as behind a desk. About Ember We're building the future of public transport — convenient, affordable, connected and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier and more enjoyable to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car. Ember is a tech company, not a traditional bus operator. We've built a platform that coordinates our entire operation — everything from monitoring vehicles and controlling chargers to selling tickets and calculating ETAs. This allows us to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world, leading to a massive reduction in emissions. It also helps us provide a much better passenger experience, with innovative features like demand-responsive stops. We’re still tiny, with a handful of routes and ~100 buses. The challenge is to scale this 50x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve recently raised a Series A from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and are looking for mission-driven individuals who want to get on board and help take us to the next level. The role Charging hubs are Ember's key growth enabler. They give us the ultra-fast charge points we need to run our network, and they act as a base for our fleet — parking, washing, driver lounges and more. We have hubs across Scotland today, with additional sites across the UK under construction or in the pipeline. You'll join a small team of four, taking end-to-end responsibility for your own sites and helping out on others. We're typically running a handful of projects at any one time. Step one is finding a site. You’ll need to think about where we need charging capacity to support future routes, scout industrial estates and brownfield plots and reach out to commercial agents, local authorities and landlords. Some great sites are advertised but many are not, so landing one usually means being patient and creative. Once you've got a site, we move on to lease negotiations, design, the planning application and the power connection. You'll work with network operators to land the grid connection, and with our suppliers to procure, install and commission the charging equipment. Solicitors, architects and engineers are there to help, but the project is yours to drive — you set the direction, you ask the difficult questions and you make the trade-offs. It’s important to be hands-on. We don't go to tender and leave the rest to an outsourced project manager — we want you on site, asking why a kerb is in the wrong place. Even after a site is live, our involvement doesn't stop. The team keeps refining and improving every site, and you'll be part of that work across the network, not just on the sites you've built yourself. Diversity and equality At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave. Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy . What's on offer You'll receive a salary of £50,000–£75,000 per annum, depending on your experience and skills, plus share options. You'll be expected to work from our lovely office in central Edinburgh most days — we value in-person communication — but there's flexibility around the odd day from home, with an expectation that you'll spend some time travelling to different sites. How do I apply? Send your CV and a short note on why this interests you. Applications close Friday 27 November at 5pm. Who we're looking for You should have a desire to get involved in the growth of a quickly scaling business, with a real opportunity to make your mark. How you work and think matters more to us than specific industry experience. The following should sound a lot like you: Curious and quick to learn. You're comfortable in unfamiliar territory — new technical specs, new legal terms, new planning processes — and you treat each one as an opportunity to learn. You don't expect to know everything on day one. Engineering mindset. You're the sort of person who'll happily watch YouTube videos explaining concrete reinforcement, three-phase distribution or substation transformers. You'll be excited to dive into the same level of detail on our projects. A first-principles thinker. You take problems back to fundamentals rather than reaching for jargon or the way things are usually done. When you work with experts — solicitors, architects, engineers — you treat them as people you can learn from, not people you can outsource your thinking to. Commercially astute. You can tell when something is worth fighting for and when it's better to redesign around a constraint, whether that's a lease, a planning condition or a contractor's quote. Highly organised. Managing a pipeline of projects is complex, with many timelines, people to chase, details to look into and things that can (and will) go wrong. We want you at Inbox Zero, not in inbox hell. Comfortable using AI. At a minimum you use it as part of how you work — to learn faster, draft documents and get to the bottom of unfamiliar topics. But maybe you’ll go further and build software to help the team work faster and more precisely. Hands-on. Hubs are built in the real world, not behind a screen. You'll meet landlords, talk to electricians and look at drains, but you'll also need to read contracts and chase agents who've gone quiet. A strong sense of what good looks like. Whatever the topic, problem or issue. You need to know how to hold yourself and others to a high standard. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

complex enterprise sales cycles (6+ months) with multiple stakeholders</li> <li>Strong ability to engage and influence executive-level buyers</li> <li>Consistent performance in pipeline generation and net new business development</li> </ul> <h4><strong>While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Experience navigating public sector procurement frameworks and compliance processes</li> <li>Background selling technical or platform-based solutions</li> <li>Ability to operate independently in a foundational, first-hire environment<br>Demonstrated success in title: Staff Analytics Engineer
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role This is a senior individual contributor role in our Data Services & Governance team where you'll act as the thought and technical leader owning the semantic layer and analytics standards for Pleo. This means that you won't own a domain but you'll own what good looks like across all of them by developing, improving , maintaining and evangelising our modelling standards and AI-augmented development practices that every Analytics Engineer work with, regardless of which team they sit in. The semantic layer you will be designing and maintaining will be the single source of truth that AI agents, BI tools, and analysts query. This is foundational work with company-wide reach which will be ideal for you if you enjoy building things from the ground up. Our semantic layer is still in very early stage. Tooling selection is live, and this role has a strong voice in it. Our BI stack is also in transition so, you would not be inheriting a mature setup and maintaining it. You'd be deciding what it should be, then building it. For additional context, our tech stack currently include: GCP, BigQuery, dbt Core, Airflow, SQL, Python, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot. Who you'll work with You'll report to the Data Engineering Manager who oversees the Data Infra & MLOps team as well as the Data Services & Governance team. Your primary relationship will be with Analytics Engineers embedded across the Intelligence function who should come to you for architecture guidance, semantic layer decisions, and standards questions. You will also partner with a Staff Data Engineer on data engineering standards and pipeline practices, and with others on self-serve analytics and BI tooling governance. You'll engage with the Data Serving team on entity definitions and with the GenAI Platform team on what AI-ready data looks like at the platform boundary. What you'll be doing Own the semantic layer: define what a metric definition is, how it's structured, where it lives, and how it's enforced. The goal is one canonical definition of Monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn, transaction, customer - used by analysts, BI tools, and AI tools without divergence. You make that real, not aspirational. Set data modelling standards for the function: what clean, layered, well-tested dbt architecture looks like across all domains, at all levels of complexity. Build and run the Analytics Engineering community of practice including code reviews, shared patterns, documentation, onboarding etc. The goal is to create a social infrastructure that makes standards stick. Own the AI-native development practice. Use AI coding tools as a native part of how you write, review, and migrate data models (not as a demonstration, but as your actual workflow). Evaluate what works in a governed data engineering context, what introduces risk, and shape how the Analytics Engineering community adopts it. Lead responsible AI-augmented migration work using AI tooling to accelerate data modelling and migrations across the Analytics Warehouse and Operational Data Platform. Design data models and metric definitions in a documented and structured manner enabling reliable consumption by AI services without human intervention. Engage upstream with backend and product engineers to drive data contract discipline and schema ownership upstream, rather than managing inconsistency downstream. Contribute to Data & AI Products for external customer-facing analytics where data modelling patterns and conversational analytics needs and capabilities grow. What you bring Deep demonstrated expertise in dbt and modelling practices: not just strong modelling, but a formed view of what modelling architecture should look like across a function. You can defend trade-offs, teach them, and enforce them in teams you don't manage. Deep BigQuery and SQL expertise, including performance, cost considerations, and the architectural challenges of complex analytical domains. Real experience owning a semantic layer (LookML, dbt MetricFlow, or equivalent). You have a point of view on what metric consistency should look like at scale, what breaks when it doesn't, and how to design it so AI tooling can consume it without degrading trust. AI-native development practice in a data engineering context. You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as a genuine part of how you work, and you can be specific about where they add real value and where they introduce risk in a governed analytics codebase. A track record of setting standards across teams you don't directly manage and making them stick by leveraging effective influencing techniques as opposed to relying on authority. Understanding of what LLMs and agentic tools need from a data layer such as how to model data, write documentation, and define metrics so that AI tools get consistent answers at runtime. Proven experience engaging credibly with backend engineers on data contracts and with senior stakeholders on what the semantic layer strategy means for the business. Why this role is a good fit for you This role is a good fit if: You can hold a standard without needing it applied perfectly, and you know which compromises are fatal and which are just untidy. You genuinely enjoy growing a community of practice through influence rather than authority and you take pride in seeing colleagues adopt and grow standards. You find the "how do we make data legible to an agent, not just to an analyst" problem interesting in its own right, rather than as a trend to keep up with. This role is not a good fit if You want to own a domain. The Intelligence teams have strong AEs doing that. This role is for someone who wants to own the standards they build to. You advise others to use AI coding tools but don't use them yourself. AI-native development is part of the mandate, not a differentiating nice-to-have. You are more comfortable being consulted than being accountable. The semantic layer and modelling standards you set have downstream consequences across the whole function and in AI features customers use. Your first 6 months By the end of your first six months, you'll have: Mapped the current state of modelling standards and the semantic layer across the function (where definitions are consistent, where they diverge, and what the highest-impact gaps are) to draft a plan the function has bought into. Contributed to the semantic layer tooling decision and begun onboarding the Analytics Engineers who'll build to it by writing documentation, running live sessions, reviewing PRs etc. Established a visible presence in the AE community of practice and become someone whose feedback in code reviews and whose opinions on architecture are listened to because they've been demonstrated, not just stated. Run your own workflow on AI coding tooling to the point where you can say clearly what the function should adopt, what it should not, and why. The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Core skills test: A technical test you'll be taking through an external platform to showcase your grasp of analytics engineering fundamentals. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute conversation-based interview aimed at deep diving into your previous experience and learning more about the team. Pleo Challenge: A live practical and technical interview designed to assess your problem solving skills as well as your technical expertise. Final interview: A 45-minutes interview with one of our senior leaders, focusing on assessing behavioural skills and values alignment. Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application: We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you—not AI—know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background. Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. This is a Staff level role at Pleo. This means it's a very senior position where you need to demonstrate experience leading technical initiatives that can have organisation-wide or cross-team impact for a tech business of 500-1000+ people. Prior experience owning a semantic layer is also a non-negotiable. Make sure your application reflects this. About your application English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us. A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails. Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us. Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you. Your data is safe.
